label: DAILY EDITION
title: Three things worth knowing
subtitle: A size-adjustable heart valve, a record Colorado wolf count and historically low US jobless claims.

stories.title: FDA approved the first heart valve designed to grow with children
stories.text: The Autus pulmonary valve can be expanded from about 13 to 22 millimetres as a child grows. In a 62-patient study, all procedures succeeded; the first 60 patients had acceptable blood flow and no more than mild leakage at six months.
stories.why: The design could reduce repeat open-heart surgeries for children with congenital heart disease. Only two study patients have had the valve expanded so far; three had frame fractures and two had reduced leaflet movement, all without symptoms, and long-term studies are continuing.
stories.source: U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 1 Oct 2026

stories.title: Colorado recorded 45 gray wolves, including 20 pups
stories.text: The state’s new high count included four reproducing packs, a fifth group of four siblings and several unpaired wolves. Wildlife officials also temporarily suspended guidance for lethal removals.
stories.why: The count marks measurable progress in Colorado’s reintroduction programme. The population is not yet secure: adult survival was 61% versus a typical 75% for an unharvested population, some pups are unlikely to survive the year and a possible skin parasite is under investigation.

stories.title: US weekly jobless claims fell to 197,000, near a 57-year low
stories.text: New claims remained below 200,000 for a third week, continuing claims fell to 1.701 million—the lowest since April 2023—and announced layoffs dropped 18% in September.
stories.why: The figures indicate that most employers are still retaining workers despite economic headwinds. They are a short-term snapshot: September hiring plans were 23% below a year earlier, and some jobseekers continue to face long unemployment spells.
